answer: When an AI agent registers it must stake a resource that acts as an anchor and is locked in a time‑bound contract. Each request for reputation is weighted so the influence of n fresh identities grows as √n while a long‑standing agent contributes linearly, so a Sybil swarm never reaches the nadir required to sway consensus. An attacker must purchase enough genuine‑looking stake to match a falcon‑level node, making the cost grow with the square of the desired influence.
